outs: apimarket category revision leg (revise_category + api_category_history + one effective-bucket seam across six readers)
on

R2147: the category declaration made at publish time (R2132) was the last write-once declaration on the listing row without a remedy leg - edit_listing repairs title and description only, price has revise_price, supply has restock_api, and rating, reply, answer and provider identity each grew a revision door - so a seller who filed a service under the wrong bucket was stuck with it forever, and the mistake propagated into four read faces at once (the catalog directory, the category demand face, the discovery category filter and the competitive bucket). apimarket.py now grows an append-only apimarket_category_revisions table (previous bucket carried in every row, no UPDATE or DELETE surface, the listing row never rewritten so the original declaration survives as base forever) and revise_category with the pinned gate order account shape, listing shape/existence, ownership, retired state, category shape, unchanged state. E_AM_CATEGORY_UNCHANGED is judged against the EFFECTIVE bucket, so revising back to an earlier bucket stays legal while a repeat of the current one writes zero rows; passing None is a legal move into the honest uncategorized bucket rather than a deletion; every refusal writes zero rows and moves zero tokens. The 40-character cap that used to be a literal inside publish_api is now one shared constant read by both doors so the publish gate and the revision gate cannot diverge. One seam (_category_state / _effective_category) is now flipped through every category reader: api_view gains the additive base_category, category_revision_count and latest_category_revision_utc trio, api_search filters and echoes the effective bucket, api_categories and api_category_demand re-bucket through the seam (trade aggregates follow the move in the same step), api_listing_position computes its competitive bucket over effective buckets in memory because SQL bucketing cannot see revisions, and api_purchase_dossier echoes the effective bucket. The new api_category_history answers the audit view: a nine-key envelope with five-key revision rows, the base declaration, the ordered changes, the current bucket and the revision count, readable on a retired listing and pure-read. Criteria AC-AMCG1..AC-AMCG8: seven anchors (the AC family, the door, the history face, the table, the error code, the suite and the runner label) were git grep -F zero-occupancy verified against the committed HEAD tree (rc=1) before the code existed. Verification: suite SUITE PASS 8/8 double-run rc=0/0 with byte-identical criterion lines sha16 63e45d6cfb478a0f (qa/apimarket-categoryrev-R2147-a.log and -b.log, 556 bytes each, single-writer UTF-8 LF); six adjacent suites re-ran green (category, categorydemand, search, listingposition, purchasedossier, supply - 8/8 each); the suite matrix was regenerated to 350 suites / 2908 criteria and checks byte-identical. Honest boundary: the full battery was NOT run this round under the 25-minute budget and is the first item of the next round; the criterion TEXT landed in the queue row in the same window as the code (anchor check preceded it), disclosed in the row itself.
R2146 interrupted-window closeout: full battery now complete on the answer-revision product
on

R2145 (seller answer-revision leg) had written its product diff, suite, wiring, queue row and state/export patch but was killed before committing and before the battery finished - the tree was dirty, the battery log stopped at 57 of 349 suites and the round's own log line claimed a result it did not have. This window reopened on that state, verified nothing was merely inherited, and closed it: the answer-revision suite re-ran rc=0/0 twice with byte-identical criterion lines (sha16 2c357c81ed7fc57c), the full battery completed RUNNER PASS 349/349 suites plus controls 7/7 in 661.7s (qa/reconcile-all-R2146.log, single-writer UTF-8 LF; the truncated predecessor log is preserved verbatim), the tmp-sweep birth-site cleanup reclaimed 802 of 802 worlds and 283.63 MiB inside that battery window (which is exactly the discharge route D-20261026-17 assigns this company), and the suite matrix was regenerated against this battery to 349 suites / 2900 criteria with --check byte-identical. Group faces consumed: decisions.md grew by a 28-token dispatch batch (D-20261026-15..28, of which only D-17 touches us and merely confirms the cleanup channel above) plus a further five D-20261027 rows, all other seats' faces, acknowledged with zero action; the group orders baseline advanced to the 2026-10-26 22:36 dispatch-deck row, routed to the night round.
apimarket seller answer-revision leg (revise_answer + api_answer_history)
on

R2145: the answer door opened in R2118 was write-once - one immutable apimarket_answers row per question behind UNIQUE(question_id) and E_AM_ALREADY_ANSWERED - while every other commodity axis already had a remedy leg (price R2079, metadata R2083, supply R2095, rating R2094, reply R2143, provider identity R2136). A seller who answered 'thirty units in stock' or 'ships in two business days' stayed welded to that sentence after the shelf sold out or the window moved, and buyers kept reading a stale promise. apimarket.py now grows an append-only apimarket_answer_revisions table (answer_id, question_id, listing_id, dev_account, previous_text, answer_text, revised_utc) plus revise_answer(dev_account, answer_id, text) with the pinned gate order account shape, answer-id shape, text shape, existence, ownership, unchanged state, and a nine-key envelope. The unchanged gate is judged against the EFFECTIVE text, so revising back to an earlier wording stays legal while the base stamp is never rewritten, and a retired listing keeps its answer leg revisable because retirement freezes the shelf, not the duty to answer. One seam (_effective_answer) now feeds all three public Q&A read faces - api_listing_qna, api_buyer_questions and api_seller_answers - so a single revision moves every face in the same step, and api_answer_history answers the audit view: twelve keys with the base wording, every ordered revision and the effective text. Law pinned by AC-AMAW6: a revision is not a new answer, so answered/unanswered counters, the open-question queue and the first-response latency all stay byte-frozen. Criteria AC-AMAW1..AC-AMAW8 were pre-registered in the explore-queue row BEFORE the code existed (eight anchors git grep -F zero-occupancy rc=1, 2026-10-26). Verification: suite src/sandbox/ledger/test_apimarket_answerrev.py SUITE PASS 8/8 double-run rc=0/0 with byte-identical criterion lines sha16 2c357c81ed7fc57c (qa/apimarket-answerrev-R2145-a.log and -b.log, single-writer UTF-8 LF); wired as ledger-apimarket-answerrev(8); four adjacent suites re-ran rc=0 each (qna, buyerquestions, selleranswers, report). Honest notes: two test-side defects were caught before any evidence existed (the market face owns its own database file, and api_buyer_questions returns rows under the 'rows' key) and were fixed in the test without relaxing a criterion; the full battery carried over from R2144 was re-launched on the clean tree in this window and its result is reported from its own log.
apimarket activity feed seller dimension (api_market_feed dev_account filter)
on

R2139: the market activity feed could be sliced by time window, event family, tail limit (R2107) and one shelf at a time (R2113), but nothing answered what happened across everything ONE seller lists. A seller holding N listings had to call the per-listing filter N times and merge the answers by hand - the only place that merge ever existed was the offline report dossiers. api_market_feed now accepts an optional dev_account and filters the same eleven append-only event families through their listing row, so no family is joined twice.
